datasets.name: NASA DEM
datasets.verbatim: We use NASA DEM, a global DEM at a spatial resolution of one arc second developed by reprocessing and void filling of Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) data (Crippen et al. 2016; NASA JPL 2020). ... Jpl NASA (2020) NASADEM Merged DEM Global 1 arc second V001. NASA EOSDIS Land Processes DAAC. https://doi.org/10.5067/MEASURES/NASADEM/NASADEM_HGT.001

datasets.name: Kodagu landslide inventory
datasets.verbatim: Following the landslides, the National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) used multiple high and medium-resolution optical satellite datasets for rapid mapping of these landslides using semi-automatic object-based methods, this data has been acquired from Bhuvan (https://bhuvan-app1.nrsc.gov.in/disaster/disaster.php#).

methods.name: ML-CASCADE
methods.summary: A semi-automated, web-based open-source tool hosted on Google Earth Engine that uses a Random Forest classifier to map landslide extent. It allows users to create landslide and non-landslide samples using pre- and post-event Sentinel-2 imagery, terrain data, and vegetation/soil indices, supporting both pixel-based and object-based (SNIC) classification.
methods.verbatim: ML-CASCADE is hosted on GEE and can be accessed from https://hydrosense.users.earth-engine.app/view/ml-cascade.

availability.author_statement: Availability statement has link for the proposed system, which maps landslides.

reproducibility_assessment: The landslide inventory is linked via the Bhuvan portal, and input datasets (Sentinel-2, NASA DEM) are accessible via public repositories. The custom ML-CASCADE code is provided via a persistent Google Earth Engine link.
